title: Shipping the MIGRO demo
speaker: Maintainer

source.speaker: Design notes
source.body: Keep the gold MIGRO icon beside the handwritten wordmark. The lettering is embedded in the banner.

source.speaker: Release notes
source.body: The repository includes portable host interfaces, reporting scripts and paired analysis tools. The earlier performance tables are frozen snapshots with their own protocols.

source.speaker: Maintainer
source.body: The frontier figure goes third, after the existing launch and architecture images.

source.speaker: Runtime guide
source.body: For the full memory runtime, install the runtime and benchmark extras and build the three C++17 coding kernels with python -m migro.backend.build_native. Set MIGRO_ASSETS to the asset root before importing the memory module.

source.speaker: Runtime guide
source.body: The Git checkout does not include the shared core checkpoint or the frozen Mistral interface. Supply those separately, along with the Qwen and Mistral model directories, matching tokenizers and reranker.

source.speaker: Release notes
source.body: The package checks covered CPU persistence, loading saved state on a receiver and appending observations. A full CUDA benchmark was not rerun for that code publication.

update.speaker: Demo notes
update.body: The interactive demo now has a local server. Start python demo/serve.py, open the local page on port 18764 and choose Edit & rerun. New answers are generated on the server. The demo server defaults to CPU.

update.speaker: Download fix
update.body: The old README download button opened raw HTML source in a browser. The replacement download is MIGRO-Handoff.zip. Unzip it and double-click MIGRO-Handoff.html to replay recorded answers offline.

update.speaker: Demo notes
update.body: The standalone HTML embeds its recorded answers and handwritten font. Editing a case offline exports session.json for use with a configured local runtime.

update.speaker: Design notes
update.body: A new animated preview belongs in the README’s Handoff section, alongside the ZIP download and instructions for running your own session.

questions: My collaborator can play the ZIP but wants to change a note and get a new answer. They only have a clean clone. What should I tell them to set up and run?
A teammate clicked the old README link and got a page of HTML. What file should I send so they can try the demo offline, and how do they open it?
I've updated the demo animation. Where should I put its preview without displacing the existing frontier figure?
Can I tell a collaborator that the release checks reproduced the full CUDA benchmark? What did those checks actually cover?
